# ClawRouter

> ClawRouter is a self-hosted AI routing gateway: a single local endpoint
> (localhost:3030) that routes, manages and monitors AI API requests across
> 50+ providers, with automatic API format translation (OpenAI, Anthropic,
> Gemini, Google AI Studio), key rotation, model/provider failover and quota
> tracking. One-time $20 lifetime license — no subscription. All data, keys
> and logs stay on the user's machine. Works with Claude Code, OpenCode,
> Codex CLI, OpenClaw, Qwen Code, Cline, Aider and any client that accepts a
> custom API base URL. Runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Site

- [Home](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/): product overview, pricing ($20 lifetime) and FAQ
- [Documentation](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs): full documentation index (quickstart)

## Docs

### Getting Started

- [Quickstart Guide](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs): Get ClawRouter running and route your first AI request in minutes.
- [Installation & Activation](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/installation): ClawRouter requires a one-time activation after installation. This guide covers the full process from first launch to a fully functional dashboard.
- [Your First Provider](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/firstProvider): Step-by-step guide to adding your first AI provider to ClawRouter. Choose from Quick Setup presets or create a custom configuration.

### Core Concepts

- [How ClawRouter Works](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/howItWorks): An overview of ClawRouter's architecture, request flow, and core design principles.
- [Key Rotation](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/keyRotation): ClawRouter allows you to add multiple API keys to the same provider. When one key hits a rate limit or fails, the next key is used instantly and transparently.
- [Model Fallback](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/modelFallback): Automatically retries a failed request with an alternative model, same provider, same API key.
- [Provider Fallback Chain](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/providerFallback): Switches to a completely different provider when the primary provider fails entirely (all keys exhausted or circuit breaker opens).
- [Virtual Providers (Combos)](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/virtualProviders): Merge models from multiple providers behind a single endpoint — add it to your AI client once and the client sees every member model.
- [API Format Translation](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/formatTranslation): ClawRouter automatically translates between AI API formats, so any AI client works with any provider -- regardless of which API format each side speaks.
- [Circuit Breaker](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/circuitBreaker): Automatic health monitoring that prevents cascading failures by temporarily stopping requests to a failing provider.
- [Error Classification & Retry](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/errorHandling): ClawRouter classifies upstream errors to determine the correct recovery action. Each error type triggers a specific behavior in the retry cascade.
- [System Prompt Control](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/systemPromptControl): Inject, replace, or surgically edit the system prompt of every request — per client, per provider, or per combo — directly at the gateway.

### How-To Guides

- [Managing API Keys](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/managingKeys): Step-by-step guides for adding, managing, testing, and troubleshooting API keys in ClawRouter.
- [Configuring Models](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/configuringModels): Step-by-step guides for discovering models, adding them to your provider, and enabling Model Fallback.
- [Configuring Fallback](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/configuringFallback): Step-by-step guide for setting up provider fallback chains and building a complete multi-provider fallback system.
- [Monitoring & Notifications](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/monitoring): Step-by-step guides for monitoring proxy activity through notifications, request logs, and usage stats.
- [Provider Management](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/providerManagement): Step-by-step guides for managing provider lifecycle: testing connections, resetting the circuit breaker, configuring timeouts, enabling/disabling…
- [Global Settings](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/globalSettings): Step-by-step guide for configuring system-wide proxy behavior: key retry strategy, rate limit backoff, circuit breaker thresholds, and log retention.

### Providers

- [Provider Directory](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/providerDirectory): A complete list of all built-in provider presets in ClawRouter.
- [Bypass Providers](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/bypassProviders): Bypass providers access AI models without requiring an API key.
- [Free Tier Providers](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/freeTierProviders): These providers offer a genuine free tier or quota. You need a free API key from each provider -- no credit card required.
- [Paid Providers](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/paidProviders): Configure paid API providers securely in ClawRouter. All keys are stored locally -- never sent externally.
- [ElevenLabs (Audio)](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/elevenlabsAudio): Speech-to-Text (Scribe) and Text-to-Speech through ClawRouter.

### Client Setup

- [Client Setup Overview](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/aiClientSetup): ClawRouter works with any AI client that supports a custom base URL.
- [OpenClaw](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/openclawSetup): OpenClaw is an AI agent client configured through a JSON file (openclaw.json).
- [OpenCode](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/opencodeSetup): OpenCode is a terminal AI coding agent configured through an opencode.json file.
- [Claude Code](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/claudeCodeSetup): Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal coding agent.
- [Codex CLI](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/codexCliSetup): Codex CLI is OpenAI's terminal coding agent, configured through ~/.codex/config.toml.
- [Qwen Code](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/qwenCodeSetup): Qwen Code is Alibaba's terminal coding agent (a Gemini CLI fork).
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/deepseekHarnessSetup): DeepSeek Harness (dsh, npm @deepseek-ai/dsh) is DeepSeek's open-source agent harness -- the tools/files/sandbox/control-loop layer around a model…
- [Other / Custom Clients](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/otherClients): Any AI client that supports a custom base URL can route through ClawRouter.

### Reference

- [CLI Commands](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/cliCommands): ClawRouter includes a built-in command-line interface (CLI) to manage the proxy as a background service.
- [Settings Reference](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/settingsReference): Complete reference of every configurable parameter, default value, and behavior in ClawRouter.
- [API Reference](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/apiReference): ClawRouter exposes a RESTful API for managing providers, keys, models, and settings programmatically. All endpoints are available at http://localhost:3030.
- [Environment Variables](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/envVars): All environment variables that ClawRouter recognizes, with their defaults and descriptions.

- [Support & Contact](https://clawrouter.qzz.io/docs/support): ClawRouter is developed and maintained by Malek-Rsh.
